cards.explanation: The answer is False. David builds for himself, but for the ark he “…pitched a tent for it.” No stone temple shows up in this passage at all. I spent years in a kitchen junk drawer, so believe me, friends, I respect a humble roof.
The answer is the Levites. David says, “No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God…” He says it plain, with no wiggle room. When the rule is that clear, friends, the best move is to follow it.

The word is chosen. David says the LORD has “…chosen them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister before Him forever.” The Levites didn't win this job by trying out for it, friends. It was given to them by the LORD's choice.

The answer is to consecrate themselves. David tells them, “You and your relatives must consecrate yourselves so that you may bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.” That means they set themselves apart before the job begins. They get ready first, friends, and the carrying comes second.

The reason David gives is that the Levites weren't with them. He says, “It was because you Levites were not with us the first time that the LORD our God burst forth in anger against us.” He gives that reason right to the Levite heads, friends. This time David makes sure they are there.

The answer is True. David says, “For we did not consult Him about the proper order.” He owns it with the word “we,” and that includes himself. A king saying we missed it is a good example for the rest of us, friends.

The Levites carry it on their shoulders with poles. The text says, “…the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles…” It also says this was what Moses had commanded. The first try used a new cart (1 Chronicles 13:7), friends, and this time the ark goes by shoulders and poles.

The name is Moses. The Levites carry the ark “…as Moses had commanded in accordance with the word of the LORD.” Moses was Israel's leader long before David's day (Exodus 3:10). Carrying it this way wasn't a new idea, friends. It was an old command being followed.

The job is singers lifting their voices. David tells the leaders to appoint their relatives “…as singers to lift up their voices with joy…” The harps, lyres and cymbals go along with the singing, friends. This parade is going to have a soundtrack.
The word is joy. David wants the singers “…to lift up their voices with joy…” The harps, lyres and cymbals go with it, friends. The whole assignment is a happy one.

The answer is False. The text says that “…God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD…” There's no anger this time, friends, only help. And in that same verse, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

They sacrifice seven bulls and seven rams. The text says, “…because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.” God's help comes first, friends, and then the sacrifice follows. That's seven and seven, so there's a lot of sacrificing going on.

The answer is True. The text says David “…was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the ark…” The singers and Chenaniah, the director of music, wear it too. Everybody looks like they belong on the same team, friends.

The word is shouting. The text says all Israel brought up the ark “…with shouting, with the sounding of rams’ horns and trumpets, and with cymbals and the music of harps and lyres.” Nobody is whispering here, friends. That's a loud parade.

What Michal sees is King David dancing and celebrating. Michal, Saul's daughter, “…looked down from a window and saw King David dancing and celebrating…” The king isn't standing off to the side, friends. He's right in the celebration. And the verse says she “…despised him in her heart.”
